paper.title: Huxley-Gödel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine
paper.central_claim: Selecting which self-modified coding agent to expand by clade-level metaproductivity (CMP, estimated from pooled descendant task outcomes) instead of the agent's own benchmark score approximates a Godel Machine acceptance rule; HGM then outperforms DGM and SICA with fewer allocated CPU-hours, and its discovered agent transfers to SWE-bench Lite and GPT-5 at the level of the best human-engineered coding agents.

evidence.quote: assuming that this implies more promising subsequent self-modifications
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated assumption under audit: expansion strategies of prior self-modifying coding agents favor higher benchmark performance, assumed to imply more promising future self-modifications.

evidence.quote: oracle is sufficient to implement the Gödel Machine.
evidence.support_explanation: Theorem 1 (Under Assumption 1) states CMP oracle access suffices to imitate the Godel Machine; it is a statement about the true CMP, not about the HGM estimator.

evidence.quote: The agent’s utility is measured by its performance on evaluation tasks, under the assumption of repeatable trials: for any agent–task pair, the expected outcome is independent of evaluation time or prior events.
evidence.support_explanation: Theory conditions: utility = final agent only, repeatable trials, proofs free, each self-modification costs exactly one budget unit (Assumption 1 bullets).

evidence.quote: aggregating evidence across a clade yields more statistically robust estimates than single-node outcomes
evidence.support_explanation: Motivation for clade pooling: CMP-hat(a) is the pooled success fraction n_success^C/(n_success^C+n_failure^C) over all evaluations in a's clade; selection by Thompson sampling with a tau scheduler.

evidence.quote: which creates a selection of a soft maximum in the clade
evidence.support_explanation: The true CMP is defined with a max over the clade (E[max U]); the estimator is an evaluation-count-weighted mean, and the paper argues the evaluation policy approximates a soft maximum. No consistency/regret bound for this approximation is given.

evidence.quote: The asynchronization also introduces another bias that favors agents with fewer evaluated results to be more often selected for evaluation than in the standard HGM.
evidence.support_explanation: Acknowledged bias in the actual (HGM-Async) implementation used in all experiments; effect size not quantified beyond the statement that it fades after ~50 evaluations.

evidence.quote: as the maximum empirical mean of the task performance achieved within its clade, with the root of this clade excluded.
evidence.support_explanation: Target for the mismatch diagnostic (empirical CMP) is a noisy extreme-value statistic of per-agent empirical means; computed on each method's own final tree.

evidence.quote: We exclude the root of a clade to avoid the circular use of the target in the estimators.

signatures.object: Parent-selection / evaluation-scheduling policy over an archive tree of self-modified coding agents (the outer loop of a DGM-style improver); baselines: DGM (score + #children sampling, progressive subset eval) and SICA (greedy best-score parent, full-set eval).
signatures.information: Per-agent counts of binary task successes/failures (own and clade-aggregated), remaining budget, tree structure. The information visible to the LLM that performs the self-modification (logs, traces) is not described here (deferred to DGM code).
signatures.operation: Thompson sampling over Beta(tau(1+n_s^C), tau(1+n_f^C)) for the expansion parent; Thompson sampling on own counts for the evaluation target; UCB-Air-style rule to expand when N^alpha >= |T| (alpha=0.6); evaluation at single agent-task granularity; asynchronous parallel execution; final best-belief agent by posterior percentile.
signatures.output: Next node to expand (child = LLM-produced self-modification of the parent's repository) or next agent-task pair to evaluate; final selected agent.
signatures.conditions: Assumption 1: repeatable trials, utility depends only on final agent, free proofs, unit modification cost; static benchmark; noisy binary task outcomes.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Thompson sampling on the same benchmark tasks that are later reported (SWE-Ver-60, Polyglot subset, full Verified); budget 800 (or 8000) task evaluations.
signatures.persistence: Archive tree retains every generated agent (code diffs), including non-improving ones; counters updated per evaluation; final agent returned.
signatures.later_use: Retained agents are parents of later children; best-belief agent is deployed to SWE-bench Lite and with GPT-5.
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher final accuracy than DGM/SICA at 800 evaluations (56.7 vs 53.3/50.0 on SWE-Ver-60; 30.5 vs 27.1/25.4 on Polyglot) with 2.38x/6.86x/1.65x fewer allocated CPU-hours; transfer to Lite.
signatures.failure_boundary: Single run per method; async bias favoring lightly-evaluated agents; SICA run crashed; selection-set results; no handling/rate of invalid children reported.

signatures.object: The acceptance/utility proxy for self-modifications: from the agent's own benchmark score to clade-metaproductivity CMP (expected best descendant utility).
signatures.information: True CMP oracle (theory) / pooled descendant outcomes (estimator).
signatures.operation: Define CMP_pi(T,a)=E[max_{a' in clade} U(a')]; prove that, in the restricted Godel-POMDP of Assumption 1, CMP equals the state-action value so an oracle suffices to imitate the Godel Machine; estimate it by the pooled clade success rate.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Table 1 diagnostic uses each method's own final tree; empirical CMP = max empirical mean over clade excluding root.
signatures.persistence: not_applicable: conceptual metric; counters live in the S1 archive.
signatures.claimed_effect: HGM estimator correlates 0.78/0.63 (weighted) with empirical CMP vs 0.29-0.44 for score-based estimators.
signatures.failure_boundary: Estimator (weighted mean) differs from the definition (max); no consistency or regret guarantee; correlation target is noisy.

gap.author_gap: DGM and SICA expand agents favoring higher benchmark performance, assuming this implies more promising self-modifications; the authors name the Metaproductivity-Performance Mismatch.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete, load-bearing selection-rule residual (which archive node to expand, under noisy partial evaluation) that was fixed by prior work and is changed here. The empirical case for the mismatch is correlational only (own-score vs empirical CMP positive at 0.29-0.44 on each method's own tree, with no node counts, noise ceiling or oracle-parent comparison); the stronger claim that score-based parent choice causes worse search is supported only by end-to-end comparison.
gap.lineage: Godel Machine (Schmidhuber 2003) -> Success-Story Algorithm / fitness-monotonic execution -> Self-Taught Optimizer / Godel Agent -> SICA (greedy best-score parent) and DGM (archive, score+children sampling, progressive eval) -> HGM (clade-level estimate, Thompson sampling, decoupled async evaluation).
gap.closest_adjacent: DGM (archive-based parent sampling by score and child count) and SICA (greedy); the paper also positions against fixed-budget BAI, MCTS/UCT and infinite-armed bandits. Archive/evolutionary LLM program-search methods that weight parents by descendant fitness are not discussed in the pinned material.
gap.residue: How to estimate and spend evaluations on descendant productivity when per-agent evaluations are few and noisy.
gap.stakes: Search cost: roughly $5000 for the reported experiments; DGM 1231-2385 allocated CPU-hours per 800 evaluations; SICA instability.
gap.method_response: Pool outcomes over the clade, sample parents with Thompson sampling, decouple expansion from single-pair evaluation, run asynchronously.
gap.remaining_gap: No ablation isolating clade pooling from Thompson sampling/decoupled evaluation/async; no seeds; estimator vs oracle CMP not bounded; self-modification step (what the improver sees) unchanged from DGM; whether the improver itself (not the selector) improves is not shown.
unresolved: Non-Godel-lineage archive/evolutionary LLM search neighbors (original text not in pinned materials): whether descendant-based parent weighting already exists there. Request: add originals of closest archive-based evolutionary agent/program search papers if G needs closing.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS C11: name the one assumption in a selection rule (here: own benchmark score predicts descendant productivity) and rebuild the rule with a certificate. RSI H20: choose archive parents by estimated descendant productivity rather than current score and archive non-improving offspring. HGM's CMP-based Thompson sampling over the clade realizes both.
pattern_mapping.required_conditions_and_differences: C11 demands a re-derived guarantee for the new rule (only oracle-level Theorem 1 here); H20 demands independent seeds and held-out certification (held-out present, seeds absent). pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Recasting self-modification acceptance as a Q-value (CMP) in a restricted Godel-POMDP is the formal bridge that licenses using clade statistics as the H20 parent-selection criterion.
